summary: What is the most common question sign in ASL. One version shakes two open hands, palms up; another slides an index finger across the other palm. Eyebrows down make it a question.
steps: Hold both hands open, palms up, in front of you.
Shake them slightly side to side with a questioning shrug.
Lower your eyebrows and lean in a little. Hold the face until you get an answer.
note: WHAT usually goes at the end of the sentence. YOUR NAME WHAT, not WHAT YOUR NAME. The eyebrows stay down on WHAT.
mistakes: Raised eyebrows. WH-questions use lowered brows; raised brows are for yes/no questions.

faq.q: Why are there two signs for WHAT?
faq.a: Both are standard. The open-hands shrug is more casual and more common in conversation; the finger-across-palm version is a bit more formal. Either is understood everywhere.
